analysis: Examined scripts/test-provider-release-pipeline.py (base 200, head 16-24, 209-215, 461-568). This file contains only unittest assertions over workflow text. It relaxes the prior invariant 'no continue-on-error in RELEASE' (base line 200) to exactly 3 occurrences. The facts step uses continue-on-error: ${{ env.CLUSTER_RUNTIME_SEND != 'true' }}. The show and retain steps use continue-on-error: true. New tests pin these properties of the cluster-runtime facts step in build-and-release: it runs after notarization and BUNDLE_HASH; it runs before the Record/Prepare/Cleanup keychain steps; it references no secrets and has no step env; it unsets r2_public_url/coordinator_url; it deletes the signing keychain and checks find-identity (non -v) before running the app CLI; it verifies the hash before extraction; and it has a 20-minute timeout. The tests also pin that provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh runs the app CLI under env -i, and that CLUSTER_RUNTIME_SEND is gated on publish plus per-environment vars. In the prepare step, the send-off path must be byte-identical to the current command, and the send-on path requires test -s plus --cluster-runtime. The artifact upload uses a pinned SHA and has no secrets. Security-relevant items that integration must verify against the actual changed files, which are not supplied in this batch: .github/workflows/release-provider.yml, scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh, and scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-models.py. 1) Executing the signed app CLI in the signing job while the runner still holds the notarytool/Apple credentials, GITHUB_ENV values, or the GITHUB_TOKEN. The tests only cover keychain removal and two unsets. 2) The models fetch script reaches the network per environment; check what it trusts. 3) Whether cluster-runtime.json fed to the publication prepare step becomes signed provenance or release metadata that the coordinator trusts. This is relevant to A-011/A-017/T-054. 4) Whether the soft-fail (continue-on-error) can let a publish proceed with stale or absent facts when the send flag is on. The tests assert that it cannot. 5) Whether the release-swift and release-dev-branch path filters include the new scripts. No regression is evident from the test file itself; it strengthens assertions.
